issues.problem: This is C2-M1's root cause in a case the fix does not cover: the script still treats any --dir strictly inside the tree as a dedicated checkpoint dir. team.checkpoint.dir is relative to the bank and set by the user (mb_team_ops.py:115). With `dir: .` (the bank itself) or `dir: ../src`, the --dir is an existing, populated dir inside the tree. Three things then happen. (1) The self-exclusion filter at :54-57 silently leaves every untracked file under that dir out of the tar, with no skipped_large entry. (2) :39 writes a `*` .gitignore into the dir. That file ignores itself, so it is invisible, and from then on new files there are hidden from git status and from mb_vcs.sh untracked. Later checkpoints and `team commit` miss new bank notes or plans, or new source files. (3) :38 chmods the dir to 700. Reproduced in the scratchpad: (a) --dir=<tree>/src gave a tar without src/work.txt, src mode 755->700, and a src/later.txt created afterwards did not appear in `git status --porcelain -uall`. (b) --dir=<tree>/.memory-bank gave a tar without .memory-bank/note.md, and note.md vanished from git status. In both cases rc was 0. The only signal is the 'contains files tracked by a repository' warning, printed after the .gitignore is already written.
issues.fix: Run the chmod 700 and the `*` .gitignore only on a dir this call created, or on an existing dir that holds nothing but checkpoint artifacts: .gitignore, *.diff, *-manifest.json, *-untracked.tar.gz, *.sha256 and the .<cid>.changed/.untracked temp files. For an existing dir strictly inside the tree that holds anything else, exit 2 before writing anything, with a message like '--dir <d> is not a dedicated checkpoint dir'. That keeps the filter safe, because it then only ever excludes the script's own files. Add a bats test: an existing tracked subdir with an untracked file inside, passed as --dir, exits 2, gets no .gitignore, keeps its mode, and the untracked file stays in git status. The default <bank>/backups/team and tests :107 and :120 are unaffected. The dir in :120 holds only an empty .gitignore.

issues.problem: A --dir that is a dangling symlink makes `mkdir -p` fail and the script exit 1 ('No such file or directory'). The header contract says exit 1 means a verify mismatch or an existing id, and 2 means usage. Nothing is written, so this is cosmetic.
